growth_signal.value: Went from a $70 million Series B in 2025 to a $200 million Series C in September 2026, taking total funding to about $300 million and valuation to $1.6 billion.

entry.idea: Tracking equipment outside cell-phone coverage normally needs pricey, dedicated satellite hardware, so Hubble Network built a network of satellites that can pick up the ordinary Bluetooth signal already inside billions of devices, so nothing new needs to be built into the device.
entry.lesson: Instead of building new hardware for a new use case, find the huge installed base of an existing chip and build the missing link that lets it reach a much bigger market.
entry.name: Hubble Network

growth.reason: Funding nearly tripled from a $70 million Series B to a $200 million Series C within about a year, with valuation reaching $1.6 billion, a clear and sourced growth signal.

market.reason: Tracking assets like equipment, containers and vehicles once outside cell coverage is a large, worldwide logistics and asset-tracking market, though it is still a specialised niche rather than something everyone buys.

tech.reason: Getting a satellite in low orbit to reliably pick up an ordinary, low-power Bluetooth signal is a genuinely new hardware and radio-engineering feat that would take years for others to replicate.

entry.twist: It works with the plain, low-power Bluetooth chip already sitting in most gadgets, so devices can become satellite-trackable with just a firmware update instead of new hardware.
entry.who_pays: Businesses that need to locate equipment, containers, or other assets beyond cell coverage pay for Hubble Network's satellite tracking service.
entry.why_now: Cell networks cover only about 15% of the Earth's land, and businesses increasingly need to track lower-value assets outside that coverage, right as cheap low-orbit satellite launches have become possible.
